current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intel 4 process node production status and capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel 4, the first EUV lithography node, delivered significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7; it moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024 for the Intel Core Ultra processor and is expected to represent an increasing portion of production in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the adoption of Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for their latest manufacturing nodes. Micron expects volume shipments of its 1γ DRAM node using EUV lithography in 2025, while Intel's Intel 4, its first EUV lithography node, moved to high-volume manufacturing in 2024 for the Intel Core Ultra processor. Both highlight EUV as a key technological step for their respective next-generation products.

sentences.text: We expect volume shipments in 2025 of our next generation of DRAM, the 1γ (1-gamma) node, which will employ EUV lithography production.

▪Intel 4, our first EUV lithography node, delivers significant density scaling and approximately 20% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 7. The Intel Core Ultra processor is our first high-volume client product on Intel 4 and began shipping to customers in 2023. Intel 4 moved to high-volume manufacturing in Ireland in 2024, and is expected to represent an increasing portion of our processor production and products in 2025.

comparisons.peer_topic: Process Technology Development Strategy and Investment
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's technology development group designs and develops new process nodes to improve performance, power efficiency, cost, and size, requiring significant ongoing capital investment in technologies like EUV lithography, gate-all-around transistors, and backside power. The company pursues incremental improvements to existing designs while developing new manufacturing technologies for upcoming nodes.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe the strategic investment and development required to advance process technologies. Micron details its progression through 1α, 1β, and toward 1γ nodes, while Intel outlines its strategy of significant ongoing capital investment in technologies like EUV lithography, gate-all-around transistors, and backside power to maintain competitiveness with foundry offerings. Both emphasize that maintaining leadership requires substantial R&D and manufacturing infrastructure investment.

sentences.text: The majority of our DRAM bit production in 2024 was on leading-edge 1α (1-alpha) and 1ß nodes.

The continued development of leading-edge nodes that are competitive with the offerings of other foundries requires significant ongoing capital investment as we pursue incremental improvements and refinements of existing transistor and layout designs and manufacturing technologies, such as EUV lithography, while also pursuing new transistor and layout designs, such as gate-all-around and backside power in our upcoming Intel 18A process node, and new manufacturing technologies, such as high-NA EUV lithography for use in our upcoming Intel 14A process node.
